stepNotes.1: The public bash, output, and kill tools resolve into a seven-file execution unit with separate registry, classifier, and helper ownership.
stepNotes.2: Command text, workdirs, expanded paths, redirects, output streams, and session-bound shell IDs define the principal trust boundaries.
stepNotes.3: Parsed commands drive permissions and path accounting before spawn; foreground and background completion both use exit/close-aware cleanup.
stepNotes.4: Current-user tildes are expanded before containment, opaque paths prompt interactively, destructive argv gets a non-persistent gate, and child environments are sanitized.
stepNotes.5: PID escalation, timeout/abort convergence, capped output, bounded observer replay, and per-session shell limits constrain runaway processes and memory.
stepNotes.6: Orchestration, background state, argv classification, pure helpers, incremental reads, and termination authority have distinct module owners.
stepNotes.7: Asynchronous best-effort failures are logged, validation catches have explicit outcomes, and the sole TODO is a naming concern rather than unfinished control flow.
stepNotes.8: Focused helper, classifier, and background tests cover 35 cases; broader bash tests exercise permission and isolation paths, with an end-to-end tilde assertion remaining desirable.
stepNotes.9: The Critical tilde finding was re-confirmed; 92 tests passed with the app isolation backend and core TypeScript checking succeeded.
